suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, and `.integration` is read on it without optional chaining. WHY: Any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar (the new `[]` or null cases) throws a TypeError in create instead of falling back to Cal Video. HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: In updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. WHY: It searches for a calendar whose externalId equals a falsy value, so it always returns undefined and the previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost. HOW: Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled by pushing inside async `.map` callbacks, and the array is then used by `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. WHY: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null (no eventType or organizer calendar), the push is skipped, so collective hosts' calendars are dropped. HOW: Build the array explicitly, `[...(main ? [main] : []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`, instead of using optional-chained push.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: In the non-credentialId branch, the loop deletes with the same `uid` and `externalCalendarId` of the current reference against every user calendar credential. WHY: With multiple calendar references, each reference now triggers deletes across all credentials, which produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` never matches and the fallback always yields undefined. Use the first destination calendar's externalId as the fallback (same in deleteEvent).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when destinationCalendar is null or empty, so accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar instead of falling back to Cal Video.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, and the code reads `.integration` on it without optional chaining. Any Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the fallback branch, `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match a real calendar. `selectedCalendar` therefore ends up undefined. The same dead lookup was added to `deleteEvent`. Fall back to the first destination calendar's `externalId` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: destinationCalendar can now be null (handleNewBooking) or an empty array (reminder, webhook and cancel handlers), so the destructured mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. Reading `.integration` on it throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings that have no destination calendar, instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining on the property read.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Destructuring the first element of an empty or null destinationCalendar array gives undefined, and `.integration` is then read without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings that have no destination calendar, which this PR now represents as `[]`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then looks up a destination calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value. It never matches, so the destination calendar fallback in updateEvent and deleteEvent is always undefined. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId, or the one matching the credential, instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: destinationCalendar is now an array that is often empty or null (many callers pass []). Destructuring [] gives undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for a Google Meet location with no destination calendar, where the old `?.` fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that falsy externalCalendarId. It therefore always yields undefined, so the old fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId is lost. The same applies to the identical change in deleteEvent. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw input list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: emails to existing attendees are treated as new-guest emails, and blacklisted or duplicate guests that were never added are still treated as new guests. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the team permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`. WHY: team admins who are not owners are denied, because owner status is required in addition to admin status. HOW: use `||`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the blacklist and duplicate checks compare the guest string case-sensitively, while the blacklist entries are lowercased. WHY: a guest such as `Blocked@x.com` bypasses the blacklist and duplicates of existing attendees that differ only in case are added. HOW: lowercase the guest before comparing, and compare against lowercased attendee emails.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist is lowercased but the guest email is compared as-is, so a guest such as 'Blocked@Example.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Lowercase the guest before calling includes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The existing-attendee check uses a case-sensitive comparison, so a case variant of an existing attendee's email is added as a duplicate guest. Compare lowercased values.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is a template string like "undefined: " and is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs. When err.message is empty or err.data is missing, the user sees a garbled toast such as "undefined: ". Build the message conditionally from err.message instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The attendees are committed to the DB before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, and that call is not guarded. If the calendar update throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests were persisted and no emails were sent. A retry then fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid because the guests already exist. Wrap the calendar update in try/catch, or order the operations so the failure does not leave this half-applied state.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The uniqueness check reads the attendees and then inserts them without a transaction or a unique constraint. Concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the filter and create duplicate attendee rows. The comparison is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case is treated as a new guest.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so a team admin who is not the owner (and an owner who is not an admin) is denied. The intent is admin OR owner; use ||.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler computes uniqueGuests (existing attendees and blacklisted emails removed) but passes the raw guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails. Existing attendees who were re-submitted are then treated as new and get a 'scheduled' email, and blacklisted addresses are treated as new too. Pass uniqueGuests.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the guest email is compared as submitted. A blacklisted address with different casing (e.g. Foo@x.com) bypasses the filter. Lowercase the guest before the includes check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded in English and bypasses the translation mechanism (`t`) used for the other strings in this component. Non-English users will see an untranslated tooltip. Use a translation key via t().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The template string is always non-empty, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs. The toast also shows a raw tRPC code prefix such as "FORBIDDEN: " to the user. Build the message from the translated error only when err.message exists, and otherwise use unable_to_add_guests.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but the Google service assigns it directly to `key` and writes it to the credential. WHY: the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the token fields, so every later `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google calendar integration breaks after the first refresh. HOW: take `.data` from the parse result, and when sync is enabled read the token from `await res.json()` instead of `res.data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed object keys that evaluate to fixed literal strings such as "ZodString", not wildcard keys. WHY: when credential sync is enabled, the schema requires a numeric property literally named "ZodString", so every refreshed response fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". HOW: use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()`, and check expiry separately if it is needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` is passed `credentialId` as its third argument, which is the Cal.com userId. WHY: with sync enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user's tokens, because the credential id is treated as a user id. HOW: pass `credential.userId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the Salesforce service now always calls the Salesforce token endpoint and updates the DB inside the connection setup, bypassing `refreshOAuthTokens`. WHY: this adds a network refresh plus a write on every connection, and it ignores credential sync. When sync is on, the stub `refresh_token` is used and the parse result may not match the stored shape. HOW: route the call through `refreshOAuthTokens` and only refresh when the token is expired.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information that can be used to recover the secret. Compare the header and secret using crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers (for example, hash both with SHA-256 first), and reject non-string header values.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), but the old code stored the value from googleCredentialSchema.parse. Now `key` is the wrapper object, so the credential key saved to the DB becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and Google auth breaks on the next use. Use the `.data` of the result (after checking success) as the key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is the Cal.com userId, but this call passes `credentialId`. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user (a credential id), so tokens for the wrong user or none are returned. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), but it is stored directly as the credential key. The key then becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and loses refresh_token and access_token at the top level, so later Google auth breaks. Store the parsed `.data` and check `.success`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string such as "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that name, so every parse fails when credential sync is enabled and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and an explicit expiry check instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId. With sync enabled, the credential id is sent to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId, so tokens are fetched for the wrong user or the call fails. Pass the credential's userId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed key. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the credential object. Now `{ key }` stores the wrapper object, which corrupts the stored Google credential. Use `.data` from the result.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of refreshOAuthTokens is now `userId`, but a credentialId is passed. In sync mode the sync endpoint receives the credential id as calcomUserId, so it looks up the wrong user's credentials. Pass the credential's userId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential sync is enabled, but this consumer (like zoho-bigin and hubspot) expects an axios response and reads `.data.error`. With sync enabled, `.data` is undefined and this throws a TypeError. The sync path must return the shape the caller expects, or the caller must parse the Response.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens takes a `userId` parameter, but this call passes `credentialId` (credential.id). With credential sharing enabled, the sync endpoint receives the credential id as calcomUserId, so the wrong user's credentials may be fetched. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The JSDoc says `appData.type` is "the app slug", but it is used as the credential `type` (e.g. "zoom_video"), not the slug. The doc misleads callers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is userId, but credentialId (credential.id) is passed. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user's tokens, because a credential id is not a user id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed data. The result object is written to credential.key, which corrupts the stored credential. It also parses the old googleCredentials rather than the refreshed token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the second OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. WHY: the deleteMany can delete email or WhatsApp reminders whose retryCount exceeds 1, if other handlers ever increment it. HOW: move the retryCount condition into an SMS-scoped branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the retryCount update in the catch block is not itself wrapped in a try/catch. WHY: if that update throws (for example because the reminder row was deleted), the exception escapes the loop and the handler. The remaining reminders are not processed and the cron run returns a 500. HOW: wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use updateMany.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says the delete only removes SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed. The new OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or date. Update the comment to describe both conditions. If the second branch should only cover SMS, add the method filter too.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retryCount > 1 delete clause is not restricted to method SMS, so the SMS cron can delete reminders of any method (email, WhatsApp) once their retryCount exceeds 1. Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to that clause to match the first clause and the handler's intent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `retryCount > 1` delete clause is not scoped to `method: SMS`, so this SMS cron can delete non-SMS reminders (email, WhatsApp) from the shared WorkflowReminder table. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that clause so the cleanup only touches SMS rows.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code list is decrypted, matched, and the whole re-encrypted list is written back with no guard. WHY: Concurrent logins using the same single-use code both pass the check, so the code can be reused. The last writer also overwrites the other's consumption, which can restore a code that was already used. HOW: Do the consume atomically, for example in a transaction with a row lock, or an updateMany that conditions on the previous backupCodes ciphertext and fails the login if count is 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the codes are read, decrypted, checked and then written back with no guard. Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the check before either write lands, so a 'single-use' code is accepted twice. Make the consume step atomic, for example by updating inside a transaction with a conditional where on the original encrypted backupCodes value and failing if no row matched.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup code is checked with Array.indexOf, which compares strings with short-circuiting equality and is not constant time. Compare against every stored code with crypto.timingSafeEqual (after checking equal lengths) and don't return early, so the comparison time doesn't leak how much of a code matched. The same pattern appears in totp/disable.ts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The default-exported component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, copy-pasted from TwoFactor.tsx, but it renders a backup code input. The name misleads readers and shows up wrongly in React devtools and stack traces, and it collides with the real TwoFactor component. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The server log message says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables 2FA and does not log anyone in. The message was copied from next-auth-options.ts and now misdescribes the failing operation. Reword it to refer to disabling 2FA with a backup code.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` now requires a third `backupCode` argument. The other consumer, `apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38`, still calls `disable(password, totpCode)`, so it fails type checking. Make `backupCode` optional (`backupCode?: string`) or update that caller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The eventTypeId filter is built as an unparenthesized `a OR b`, and a single filter is returned as-is from the public getFilterConditions. WHY: Any caller that combines it with `AND` without wrapping it gets the wrong SQL precedence, which would silently widen results beyond the filter and the authorization conditions. HOW: Wrap the whole expression in parentheses.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` (NOTHING_CONDITION) branches in getBaseConditions can never execute. Drop them and keep only the auth-and-filter and auth-only cases.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into an inline JavaScript string literal. WHY: the controller checks only the referer's host, so a referer path or query containing `'` and script text breaks out of the string and runs JS on the Discourse origin (XSS). HOW: build the target origin from the validated host, such as `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and emit it with `to_json` or `j()`, not the raw referer.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place. WHY: if the string is frozen it raises FrozenError. Callers that reuse the string, such as the feed loop, also get the footer appended to their own copy. HOW: use `contents = contents + "..."` so the original string is untouched.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) satisfy `start_with?('/')`, and the leading slashes are then stripped. The result is `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which points at the wrong host and breaks the link or image. Skip values that start with `//`, or prefix them with the scheme instead of the host.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The origin check uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, so any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. a truncated hostname) is accepted. Compare the origin for exact equality against the origin derived from discourseUrl.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The import footer interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute and text without escaping. Because raw_html posts skip cooking and are rendered with `raw post.cooked`, a feed link containing a quote or markup breaks out of the href and injects content. Escape the url with ERB::Util.html_escape before building the link.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The feed_polling_url and embed_by_username tests leave feed_polling_enabled? at its default of false, so poll_feed is never called whatever the other guards do. Stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, and stub the other two settings to valid values, in each test so that only the setting under test blocks the call.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: absolutize_urls treats any href/src starting with '/' as host-relative, so protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png, which breaks the link or image. Skip values that start with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme instead).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element, which is common for RSS items that only have a description. The exception aborts the whole poll, so every later item is skipped and, with retry disabled, the failure repeats every hour. Skip or fall back to the description when content is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The check for an existing embed and the later create are not atomic. PollFeed and RetrieveTopic can run concurrently for the same URL, and both can see no embed. Each then creates a topic and post, and the second `create!` raises on the unique embed_url index, leaving an unhandled exception. Handle ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique by rolling back and returning the existing embed's post, or take a lock keyed on the URL.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Disqus import used to create each topic locally with PostCreator. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches the thread link over HTTP via open(url).read with no error handling. A dead or slow link, or a non-HTTP link, raises and aborts the whole import loop. Rescue errors per thread and skip or log that thread.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The layout links the 'embed' stylesheet, but 'embed.css' and 'embed.js' are not added to config.assets.precompile in config/application.rb. In production, stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' will raise an asset-not-precompiled error, or the file will 404, so the embed page breaks. Add 'embed.css' and 'embed.js' to the precompile list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: category_fabricator.rb was overwritten with the :embeddable_host fabricator, and the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. WHY: `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` is now defined twice, and the category fabricators sit in a misnamed file. Fabrication may raise DuplicateFabricatorError, which would break the whole spec suite. HOW: Restore the category fabricators in category_fabricator.rb, and keep only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased column with the URI host without lowercasing the URI host. WHY: Ruby's URI preserves the case of the host, so a referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches a stored host, and embedding is wrongly denied. HOW: Use `host.downcase` in the query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` use `.first` on the lookup and then call methods on the result without a nil check. WHY: an unknown id raises NoMethodError, which returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])`, or raise Discourse::NotFound when the record is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The migration indexes `[0]['id']` and `[0]['value']` on query results without checking that rows exist. WHY: A site without an embed_category setting returns an empty result, so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the migration fails. The raw interpolation of `h` into the INSERT also breaks on quotes or blank lines. HOW: Guard with `.first`/`cmd_tuples` checks, skip blank hosts, and escape values with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The DB side is lowercased with lower(host), but the host parsed from the referer or URL is not downcased. Mixed-case hosts (for example http://EvilTrout.com) therefore fail to match an allowed host. Downcase the parsed host before querying so both sides are normalized.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The query lowercases the column (`lower(host)`) but compares it to `uri.host` without lowercasing it. Hosts with uppercase letters in the referer or embed URL will never match, so legitimately embeddable hosts are rejected. Downcase the parsed host before querying.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now holds the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, etc.). The embeddable_host fabricator ended up in category_fabricator.rb. The contents of the two files are swapped, so each file name misdescribes what it defines. Restore the category fabricators to category_fabricator.rb and put the :embeddable_host fabricator here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The spec title says "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but expandable_first_post? no longer checks embeddable hosts. The example now passes only because has_topic_embed? is false, so the title misdescribes what is tested. Rename it, or remove the example.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test no longer stubs has_topic_embed? or sets embed_truncate, so expandable_first_post? returns false because the built topic has no embed, not because no embeddable host exists. It would pass whatever the host table contains. Remove it, or stub has_topic_embed? and embed_truncate so that the host state is the only variable.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The before_validation callback calls sub! on self.host without a nil guard. A request that omits the host param, or EmbeddableHost.new, raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?`, or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: update and destroy use `.first` and then call methods on the result. An unknown id gives nil and raises NoMethodError, a 500 instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])`, which raises RecordNotFound, or add an explicit nil check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration indexes `[0]['id']` on the result of the embed_category lookup. When no row matches, `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, so it fails on installs where embed_category was never set. The same pattern applies to the uncategorized_category_id fallback. Check the result before indexing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration indexes `[0]` on query results that can be empty. When no `embed_category` row exists (the default), `execute(...)[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. Use `.first` with a nil guard (e.g. `row = execute(...).first; category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0`), and do the same for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `self.downsize` is defined twice, and the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) overrides the first (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). WHY: existing callers such as `resize_emoji.rb` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) now pass 5 arguments to a method that takes at most 4, so they raise ArgumentError and emoji resizing breaks. HOW: keep one definition that handles both call styles, for example `def self.downsize(from, to, *args)` that takes the opts hash from the end and builds dimensions from either one string or width and height. Alternatively, update the emoji caller to pass "100x100" and remove the dead first definition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The size limit is hard-coded to 10MB for every upload type, but only images are auto-downsized. Non-image uploads such as attachments are still limited by their site setting (max_attachment_size_kb). The file_too_large alert therefore shows a wrong limit, and oversized attachments pass the client check. Keep the site setting for non-images and use 10MB only for images.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `self.downsize` is defined twice, and the second definition `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` replaces the first `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`. The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb now passes 5 arguments to a method that takes at most 4, so it raises ArgumentError. Keep one definition that handles both call forms, or update the emoji job to pass "100x100".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` redefines the earlier five-argument `downsize`, so only the new signature exists. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: totalPages is computed as floor(user_count/limit)+1, which overcounts by one page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. WHY: the pager shows a phantom empty last page, showingLast is never true on the real last page, and 'next' loads an empty member list. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the members endpoint takes a client-supplied `limit` with no upper bound and now applies it to all groups. WHY: a request with a very large limit loads and serializes every member of a big group in one response, and a negative limit or offset can cause a database error. HOW: clamp the limit, e.g. `limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min`, and use `[params[:offset].to_i, 0].max` for the offset.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, which overcounts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 gives 2 pages). The 'next' control stays enabled on the real last page and leads to an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, which over-counts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. The pager then shows an extra page, showingLast is never true on the real last page, and "next" loads an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count/limit).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The public members endpoint now always applies a default limit of 50. It previously limited only automatic groups, so non-automatic groups returned all members. The public group members page (group/members.hbs via group-members route) was only switched to `members` and has no next/previous paging, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated. Add pagination to the public page, or keep the old unlimited behaviour for it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages uses floor(count/limit)+1, so with exactly 50 members it reports 2 pages. showingLast is then never true on the real last page, and 'next' navigates to an empty page (offset == user_count). Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: limit and offset are taken from params and passed to the query unchecked. A negative value makes PostgreSQL raise an error, so the endpoint returns a 500. Clamp offset to >= 0 and limit to a sane range.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Fallback locales are only loaded through the explicit ensure_loaded! call in ApplicationController, while translate still loads only config.locale. WHY: Translations run outside a controller request (jobs, mailers, console) never load the site default locale or :en, so fallback lookups find nothing and return missing-translation output. HOW: Have translate call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load every locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) instead of relying on the controller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, and the key is never removed when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. WHY: the next request from a rejected device within the 29-minute cache TTL returns nil at the cache check, so TagDevice succeeds and the device is authenticated as anonymous, bypassing the limit. HOW: set the cache key only after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or delete the key when it returns an error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the device limit is enforced by a separate CountDevices call followed by an unconditional upsert, with no transaction or lock. WHY: concurrent requests from new devices (or multiple Grafana instances) all read count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. HOW: do the insert conditionally in a single statement, e.g. INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit, or wrap count and insert in one transaction.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TagDevice now runs synchronously inside Authenticate. For every new device it executes a COUNT query and a write on the request path, and the earlier background goroutine with its timeout is gone. WHY: anonymous requests are blocked on DB latency, and a burst of new device IDs adds a COUNT per request. HOW: keep tagging async when no limit is configured, and only block when deviceLimit > 0. Cache the count briefly to cut the per-request COUNT queries.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Device tagging used to be a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout context and a panic recover. It now runs synchronously inside Authenticate using the request ctx. Every anonymous request's authentication now waits on the DB count and write, and a canceled request context aborts the tagging. A panic in TagDevice is no longer recovered either. Keep the tagging work off the request path or give it a bounded detached context, and only block when the device limit actually has to be enforced.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The device limit is enforced with a separate count query followed by an insert, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example by doing both in one transaction/statement (INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit) or by holding a lock.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After acquiring the write lock, the cache is not re-checked. WHY: when the cache is cold, every goroutine that missed it reloads and re-parses the manifest serially, and in Dev mode every call takes the exclusive lock for file I/O. HOW: add a second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock (skipped in Dev) before loading.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cache is assigned `result` unconditionally, even when loading failed and `result` is nil. WHY: a transient read error overwrites a previously valid cache entry with nil, and the nil is returned to the caller. HOW: assign to the cache only when `err == nil`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The shouldInstrumentRequestSize=false cases never assert that the request size metric is absent. If CheckHealth or CollectMetrics started recording request size, the test would still pass. Add an else branch asserting CollectAndCount(promRegistry, metricRequestSize) == 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The traceID log param was removed and the code now relies on FromContext to supply it. A grep found no traceID handling in pkg/infra/log, so the Plugin Request Completed log may lose its traceID. Verify that FromContext adds the trace ID, or keep adding it from tracing.TraceIDFromContext.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy goroutines derive their timeout context from the request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). WHY: The request ctx is cancelled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, so the legacy write is frequently cancelled mid-flight and legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage. HOW: Build the goroutine context from a detached parent, e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (Go 1.21+), and then apply the 10s timeout.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: DeleteCollection records the legacy delete duration with recordStorageDuration. WHY: Legacy timings and errors are attributed to the storage metric, which corrupts both series. HOW: Call d.recordLegacyDuration here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Create or Storage.Update fails, the code records the failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. WHY: Storage errors are reported on the legacy metric, so the legacy series is skewed and storage failures are missing from the storage series. HOW: Use recordStorageDuration in both error branches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Delete passes `name` as the kind label to recordStorageDuration on success, while every other path passes options.Kind. WHY: Each deleted object name creates a new label value, which gives the metric unbounded cardinality and splits the series. HOW: Pass options.Kind.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Delete stores the base logger d.Log in the context instead of the request-scoped `log`. WHY: Downstream logs lose the name, kind and method values that every other method propagates. HOW: Use klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The goroutine derives its context from the request ctx, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, so the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is frequently aborted. Legacy storage then silently diverges from unified storage. Detach the context with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the 10s timeout.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded via recordStorageDuration, so legacy timing and errors are attributed to unified storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The failed d.Storage.Create is timed with recordLegacyDuration, so the metric is attributed to legacy storage even though the call was made to unified storage. Use recordStorageDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The failed d.Storage.Update is timed with recordLegacyDuration, so the metric is attributed to legacy storage. Use recordStorageDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success path passes `name` where the kind label belongs, while the error path uses options.Kind. This creates one metric label series per object name. Use options.Kind.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy write was moved into a goroutine, but its context is derived from the request ctx, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns. Legacy writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) can therefore be aborted partway, leaving legacy storage out of sync. Derive the context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the timeout.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Previously legacy Update was given an updateWrapper carrying the object produced by the storage update. Now the raw objInfo is passed, so legacy recomputes the update against its own old object and can diverge from storage. Wrap it again with updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The old code ignored a NotFound from storage and still deleted from legacy. Now any storage error returns early, so an object that exists only in legacy can never be deleted in mode 3.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration. Legacy was never invoked, so the failed storage call is attributed to the legacy metric. Use recordStorageDuration here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When Storage.Update fails, the code records the failure with recordLegacyDuration. The failed call belongs to storage, so the legacy metric is wrong. Use recordStorageDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration. This mixes legacy timings into the storage metric. Use recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success path of Delete passes the object name where the kind label is expected. Every other call passes options.Kind. This creates one metric series per object name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy-store errors are now dropped without being logged. This is an observability problem: failures from the legacy store become invisible. Log these errors, as the previous code did.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Delete method puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log (the one with kind, name, method and resourceVersion). This is a logging-context bug: downstream log lines lose the enriched fields. Put the enriched log into the context instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy writes in Mode3 run in a background goroutine, and the tests neither wait for it nor assert that the legacy mock was called. Storage and legacy share one mock.Mock, so the setupLegacyFn expectations are never checked. The tests would still pass if the legacy write were removed. Use separate mocks, or wait on a channel or use assert.Eventually, then call AssertCalled on the legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection methods.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: BuildIndex no longer holds any lock while creating the index, and the cache is only locked for the final write. WHY: concurrent builds for the same key (init workers plus getOrCreateIndex) can both call bleve.New on the same directory, so the second fails with 'path already exists'. Both can also overwrite each other's cache entry and leak the losing index. HOW: re-check the cache under the lock before building, or serialize builds per key (a per-key mutex or singleflight), and close the losing index if one is discarded.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cacheMu lock was removed from the whole BuildIndex and now guards only the final map write. Two concurrent builds for the same key can both create an index, for example bleve.New on the same directory, and the later one overwrites the cached entry and leaks the earlier index. Re-check the cache under the lock (or use per-key singleflight) before creating the index.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: NewResourceServer now runs Init eagerly. Constructing the server blocks on search index build and storage init, and it returns (nil, err) when they fail. Callers that used to construct the server and call Init separately, such as the tests in apistore/watcher_test.go and sql/test/integration_test.go, still call Init a second time. Other consumers were not updated for the new error and blocking behaviour. Either make the double Init safe and idempotent, or remove the separate Init calls and update the callers.

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities grants Duplicate, based only on Grafana create permission, even when the rule is undefined (skipToken). WHY: AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability, so cloud/Mimir rules show a Duplicate action for users with Grafana create permission, even when the ruler is unsupported. WHY: Federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable, so Edit/Delete/Pause become available for them. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When the rule is undefined (skipToken), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed under the Grafana create permission. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability, so a cloud (Mimir) rule gets a Duplicate action based on the wrong datasource's permissions. Make every ability NotSupported when `rule` is undefined.

The old check `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule` covered both rule types. Recording rules therefore lose Pause, Export, Restore and DeletePermanently. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable is computed with prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The federated-rule-group check (isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)) was replaced with a hardcoded `false`. useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to pass the real value, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can now be edited or deleted. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isAccessTokenId returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, because the condition is inverted. The substring offsets are also wrong: the shortcut sits at indexes 4-6, but the code reads (3,5). WHY: every correct token ID fails the matcher, and the tests that use it (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and others) fail. HOW: negate the condition and use substring(4, 6).

suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant shortcut check uses substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6) and returns false when the shortcut matches. Correct ids are therefore rejected and ids with a wrong grant are accepted. Use the correct offset and negate the condition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The check returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, so it is inverted. It also uses substring(3,5), but the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-6 of the 6-char prefix. Use `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fourth requireNonNull checks grantType again, so a null rawTokenId is accepted. Check rawTokenId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The matcher returns false when the shortcut equals the expected value, so a correct token id would be rejected once the indices are fixed. The condition must be negated.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The matcher claims to verify the grant shortcut, but it returns false when the shortcut equals the expected one. It also reads indices 3..5, while the token ID format `sessionType(2) tokenType(2) grant(2)` puts the grant at indices 4..6. Fix the comment, drop the negation, and use substring(4, 6).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third null check tests grantType again while its message says rawTokenId. rawTokenId is never validated, and a failure would report the wrong field. Check rawTokenId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant shortcut is at chars 4-6 of the encoded id, but the matcher inspects substring(3,5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut. The grant type is therefore never verified, and the matcher would pass with the wrong grant encoded. Use substring(4,6) and return false when it does NOT equal the expected shortcut.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The factory's sessionFactory is null in this test, so the unknown-shortcut lookup throws an NPE instead of the intended IllegalArgumentException. The test catches RuntimeException, so it passes without validating the unknown grant branch. Catch IllegalArgumentException and set up sessionFactory (for example, a mock that returns an empty stream).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant shortcut sits at chars 4-6 of the token id, but the matcher reads substring(3,5) and returns false when it equals the expected value. The grant check is both misaligned and inverted, so wrong grants pass and correct ones can fail. Use substring(4,6) and return false when it does not equal the expected shortcut.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoder writes the token id as sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShortcut(2), so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6). The matcher reads substring(3,5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut, so it rejects correct ids and accepts wrong ones. Use substring(4,6) and negate the comparison.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reader thread is never joined before the assertion on caughtExceptions. WHY: A read still in flight when deletedAll is set can fail after the assertion has run, so the regression test can pass without detecting the concurrency bug. HOW: Keep the Thread reference, call join() after deletedAll.set(true), and only then assert.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reader thread is never joined and there is no guarantee it overlaps with the deletes. The assertion can run before the reader has done any read, or before an in-flight read throws, so the test passes even if the NPE/race bug is reintroduced. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...), which now always throws UnsupportedOperationException when V2 is active, because MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2. WHY: if the V1 feature (the new gate) and V2 are both enabled, deleting any client throws inside the event listener and can abort the client removal. suggestions.suggestionContent: The Javadoc on void requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true". The method returns nothing and throws ForbiddenException. Change the comment to "Throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false."

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: error_ids are zipped with `events.values()` by position. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Neither `age` nor `timestamp` is required, and the mutual-exclusion validators only run when the field is present and use truthiness. WHY: a report with neither field, or with `age: 0` alongside a timestamp, passes validation although the spec requires exactly one. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The hook now returns `data` from useQuery, which is undefined until the first fetch completes (and the previous value is also undefined then). WHY: consumers that expect a TagCollection object get undefined instead of the `{}` the old implementation returned, which can crash on key access. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: With the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag on, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty `columns` and empty `tableData`, ignoring `result`. WHY: every table widget renders empty when the flag is enabled. HOW: build tableData and columns from `result.data` and `result.meta`, or keep the old renderer until that is wired.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The default for `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` changed from "low" to "off" (also in constants.py). WHY: projects that never set the option silently lose automatic autofix, a behavior change unrelated to the replays bulk-delete feature in this PR. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: error_ids are zipped positionally with events.values(), but nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi returns values in the same order as error_ids and with no missing nodes. Dict order or omitted keys mismatch event ids with data. Look up each node_id explicitly instead.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, so age=0 or timestamp=0 is treated as absent and a report containing both fields is accepted. Check key presence instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The number-type test mocks the endpoint with a matcher on `query.query`, but the hook sends `substringMatch`, so the mock can never match. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: kill() and terminate() are gated on `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but the processes are `SpawnProcess` instances from the spawn context, which do not subclass `multiprocessing.Process`. WHY: the check is most likely always False, so a hung flusher process is never killed before its replacement starts, which leaves duplicate flushers for the same shards. The same check in join() means processes are never terminated on shutdown. HOW: check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: join() breaks out of the loop once the deadline passes, so `terminate()` is skipped for the current and all remaining processes. WHY: flusher processes that are still running at shutdown are left alive, since they are daemons but may be stuck. HOW: do not break. Always call terminate on every process, and use a per-process wait bounded by the remaining time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op at the top of the test, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait and the flusher thread may not have flushed before join() and the `messages` assertion. suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug

Existing Integration rows whose metadata has no "sender" (for example the webhook has not arrived yet, or the row is older) now raise KeyError and return a 500, where this path used to proceed to next_step(). suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (an unhandled 500) when the existing Integration's metadata has no "sender" entry, for example older integrations or ones not created from the installation webhook. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `end` is computed with the same expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never be true unless `start` already is. WHY: slots that start inside working hours but run past the end of them are treated as available, so round-robin fixed hosts can be booked outside their hours. HOW: compute `end` from `slotEndTime`, and convert both times to the organizer timezone before comparing them with `startTime`/`endTime`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The date override check compares two dayjs objects with `===` and uses `utcOffset * -1`, which is the wrong sign for converting organizer-local time to UTC. WHY: the `===` comparison is never true, and the sign error makes the override day and time window wrong for hosts away from UTC. Slots can then be accepted or rejected incorrectly. HOW: use `.isSame()`, and convert with `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone)` or a correctly signed offset.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it equals `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` check is meaningless. Slots that start inside working hours but run past the end are not rejected. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it duplicates `start` and does not hold the slot's end time. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check therefore never tests where the slot actually ends, and a slot that runs past working hours is not flagged. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` test never checks the slot's actual end, and slots that run past working hours are accepted. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Two distinct dayjs instances are compared with `===`, which compares references and is always false. A date override with start equal to end (the unavailable-all-day case) is therefore never recognised. Compare with `.isSame()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The working-hours check uses `find` and returns false if the slot is outside ANY single entry for that day. A day with multiple ranges, such as split shifts, therefore rejects every slot. `end` also duplicates `start`, and the comparison uses UTC time against schedule-timezone minutes. Treat the slot as available if it lies within at least one entry (`some`), converting the slot start and end to the schedule timezone first.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `getSlots` now depends on `override.timeZone`, but the field is optional on the shared `TimeRange` type. An override without it passes `undefined` to `dayjs.tz`, which probably uses the server's default timezone and gives a wrong offset. Fall back to the organizer timezone, or make the field required for overrides passed to `getSlots`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `forEach(async ...)` does not await its callbacks, so the `await getCalendar(...)` and the following `deleteEvent` run detached from the surrounding try/catch. WHY: the reschedule flow continues and responds before the calendar events are deleted, and a failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught. HOW: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))`, or a `for...of` loop with `await`. The same change is needed in the vital and wipemycalother reschedule.ts files.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the recurring-event cancellation path still uses `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})`, and the callback now awaits getCalendar. WHY: the awaits inside it are not awaited by the handler, so the calendar updates can run after the handler returns, and any rejection is unhandled. HOW: replace it with `for (const credential of ...)` using await, or `await Promise.all(map(...))`.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the appStore object holds `import(...)` promises, which start loading all 29 app modules as soon as index.ts is evaluated. WHY: this defeats the goal of lazy loading, because every app module is still loaded on first import. A rejected import is also an unhandled rejection at module load. HOW: make each entry a thunk, `() => import("./x")`, and call it only when the app is needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `forEach(async ...)` callback discards the promises, so the enclosing try/catch no longer catches errors from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`. These errors become unhandled rejections, and the handler can return before the calendar deletes finish. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all(...)` inside the try block.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The forEach callback was made async, so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent calls are not awaited by the caller. Rejections escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled promise rejections, and the reschedule continues before the calendar deletions finish. Collect the promises and await them, for example `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cancel loop sits in one try/catch and the DB deletes are only awaited after the loop, so one failed SendGrid request aborts the whole batch. WHY: Reminders already cancelled in SendGrid are never deleted, and later reminders are skipped, so cancelled emails can still be sent and the same rows are retried on every cron run. HOW: Wrap each iteration in its own try/catch and delete the DB row right after its successful cancel request.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The delete helpers are async and now do the DB write (mark cancelled or delete) themselves, but they are called without await and are no longer part of Promise.all. WHY: The handler can respond before the reminder is flagged as cancelled, particularly on serverless, so the reminder email or SMS is still sent for a cancelled booking. HOW: Collect the returned promises and await them with the other promises.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag are misnamed. With `immediateDelete=true` it only cancels the SendGrid batch and returns, without deleting the DB row. Otherwise it only sets `cancelled: true`, and deletion is left to the cron job. Callers such as the workflow-delete path read this as deleting the reminder. Rename them (e.g. `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` / `immediateCancel`) or make the behaviour match the name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. The handleNewBooking reschedule caller passes true on the assumption that the reminder is removed, as deleteScheduledSMSReminder does. The old booking's email reminder rows therefore stay in the DB, neither deleted nor flagged cancelled, so the cron never cleans them up. Delete the row after the cancel request.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled. The row stays in the database as scheduled, and the cron cleanup only matches cancelled=true rows, so it is never removed. This is reachable on reschedule in handleNewBooking, which passes immediateDelete=true. Delete the row after the cancel request succeeds.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: All cancellations share one try/catch, so a single failing SendGrid cancel request aborts the loop before any DB deletes run. The same poisoned row is retried on every cron run and blocks every later cancelled reminder, which can then be sent despite the cancellation. Wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and delete or skip it individually.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reminder cleanup used to be awaited through the Promise.all of the prisma deletes. The managers now do the DB delete or update themselves, but the handler calls them without await, so the booking cancellation can return before the reminders are cancelled or deleted. Collect the returned promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object and relies on Prisma's @updatedAt to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma generally does not write @updatedAt when the update payload has no fields, so the call is likely a no-op that still costs a DB round-trip on every cache refresh. HOW: Pass an explicit `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`, or remove the call, since the UI reads the CalendarCache updatedAt instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale, so users of other languages see US-style dates instead of their own locale format. Use the user's locale from useLocale (i18n.language) instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `should_block?` matches the email with an exact, case-sensitive lookup, so `Bad@SpamClub.com` does not match a stored `bad@spamclub.com`. WHY: a blocked address can be bypassed by changing the case when signing up. HOW: normalise case on both store and lookup, for example `where('lower(email) = ?', email.to_s.downcase)`, and downcase the email in `set_defaults`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `match_count` is incremented in Ruby (`+= 1`) and then saved, which is a non-atomic read-modify-write. WHY: concurrent signups with the same email overwrite each other's increments, so the tracked block counts are wrong. HOW: use an atomic SQL update such as `BlockedEmail.update_counters(record.id, match_count: 1)` and set `last_match_at` in the same statement.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: should_block? matches with an exact, case-sensitive comparison, so a blocked address can be re-registered by changing its case (e.g. Bad@Spammers.org). Normalize both sides, for example by downcasing on save and querying with the downcased email or using LOWER(email) = ?.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The match_count update is a read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; save`), so concurrent signups with the same blocked email overwrite each other's increment and the count undercounts. Use an atomic SQL update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now])`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The lookup `where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (e.g. `Bad@spamclub.com`), which breaks the block invariant. Normalize both sides, for example by downcasing on save and in the lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
